output_text: "A memorial plaque honoring 27 local people who died fighting in the Spanish Civil War has been unveiled at the Unite building in Islington, named after trade unionist Jack Jones, who survived the conflict and became the leader of the Transport and General Workers' Union. Local historian Danny Payne notes that 30 people from Merseyside are believed to have died, traveling secretly to Spain due to the UK government's ban on fighting in the war. The plaque now has a permanent home at the Jack Jones building, fittingly located in the same city where the war took place."
